previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma on chemotherapy, was admitted with high fever, cough, and fatigue. He developed delirium, which resolved with treatment. Blood cultures identified E. coli bacteremia, and stool testing confirmed C. difficile infection. He was treated with IV meropenem, later transitioned to ertapenem via PICC, and oral vancomycin for C. diff. Imaging showed stable biliary stents, no source of infection was definitively identified, and brain imaging ruled out metastasis or acute intracranial pathology. His condition improved, mental status normalized, and he was discharged to extended care to complete antibiotic therapy with follow-up planned.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with cholangiocarcinoma s/p 3 
cycles of Cis/Gem (last dose on ___ C3D8) who presented 
with altered mental status after recent admission for e.coli 
bacteremia and c.diff.

ACUTE CARE
# Altered mental status: Concern high for stroke initially but 
exam non focal with motor and sensory intact and MRI brain 
without abnormalities. Neurology consultants did not feel that 
there was a central explanation for his change in mental status 
and EEG was also negative. MRI did not show signs of metastatic 
disease to the brain so neuro-oncology was only involved 
initially.
He was felt to be slightly disinhibited and slightly manic, thus 
psychiatry was consulted, but their opinion was that this was 
not a psychiatric disorder due to the patient's lack of psych 
history, very unlikely to have initial presentation at age ___. 
Infectious disease was also re-consulted and they did not feel 
that infection or antibiotic side effect could account for this 
presentation. Thus, no LP was done.
Ultimately, it was felt that he patient had delirium which was 
secondary to a combination of frontotemporal dementia which was 
unmasked with the stresses of chemo, bacteremia, c.diff, 
antibiotics, hospitalization, and cancer. He did have some signs 
of  white matter changes in the frontal regions of the MRI. 
Thus, he was started on olanzapine and he was much improved back 
to his baseline at time of discharge.

# E. Coli bacteremia: from prior hospitalization, presumed to be 
cholangitis source. ID following; Ertapenem or meropenem until 
___.

# C.diff diarrhea: resolved diarrhea. Treatment course scheduled 
through ___ he was continued on PO vanco while he is being 
treated with meropenem and for 2 weeks 
following completion of ertapenem/meropenem, until ___.

increased side effects with most recent dose on ___. With 
his AMS, may need to recalculate performance status to see if 
this will affect outpatient chemo.

radiology_notes.text:
AP CHEST, 6:52 P.M., ___  

HISTORY:  A ___ man with delirium.  Possible pneumonia.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Mild left basilar plate-like atelectasis has improved since ___.  Lungs
are otherwise clear.  Cardiomediastinal and hilar silhouettes and pleural
surfaces are normal.  Right PIC line ends at the origin of the SVC.  No
pneumothorax or appreciable pleural effusion.

STUDY:  MRI OF THE HEAD WITH AND WITHOUT CONTRAST.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ man with word finding difficulties and
history of cholangiocarcinoma, evaluate for stroke or metastatic disease.

COMPARISON:  Prior MRI of the brain dated ___, prior head CT
dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Pre-contrast axial and sagittal T1-weighted images were obtained,
axial FLAIR, axial T2, axial magnetic susceptibility and axial
diffusion-weighted images.  The T1-weighted sequences were repeated after the
administration of gadolinium contrast in axial T1, sagittal MP-RAGE and
multiplanar reconstructions were reviewed.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the most recent examination, no significant
changes are demonstrated in this short interval, there is no evidence of
intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect.  There is no evidence of abnormal
enhancement to indicate metastatic disease.  No diffusion abnormalities are
detected.  Unchanged foci of high signal intensity are redemonstrated in the
subcortical and periventricular white matter, likely consistent with changes
due to small vessel disease, the major vascular structures demonstrates normal
flow void signal and distribution.  The orbits are unremarkable, the paranasal
sinuses and the mastoid air cells are clear.

IMPRESSION:  No significant changes are demonstrated since the most recent
study, there is no evidence of acute or subacute intracranial process.  There
is no evidence of abnormal enhancement to suggest metastatic disease.  Foci of
high signal intensity identified in the subcortical and periventricular white
matter on T2 and FLAIR sequences are likely consistent with changes due to
small vessel disease.
